# Permavia Landscapes

> Permavia Landscapes is a regenerative development company serving clients across East Africa. We design, build and manage nature-positive landscapes and productive systems that restore ecosystems, strengthen livelihoods and create lasting value for communities, putting nature-based methods first. The first 30-minute discovery call (on Webex) is free.

## Key facts
- Area served: East Africa (contact address: Hoima City, Uganda)
- Services: Regenerative Design; Installation of Regenerative & Community Development Projects; Farm Solutions; Maintenance; Education for Regenerative Design & Management
- Projects: Million Trees (Tree Nursery, Underway: Establishing); Permavia Farm (Regenerative Demonstration Farm, Planning); Permavia Academy (Learning Platform, In Development)
- Methods: nature-based first. Regeneration is treated as a process: machinery and limited, targeted inputs may be used to establish systems on large or degraded land, then phased out as the land regenerates itself
- Opening hours: Mon to Sat, 8am to 6pm (EAT)
- Contact: phone/WhatsApp +256 394 777 418; email info@permavialandscapes.com; website https://www.permavialandscapes.com/
- Free discovery call: book at https://www.permavialandscapes.com/contact/#book

## Services
- [Regenerative Design](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/services/regenerative-design/): Site assessment and a complete design for water, soil, plants and people.
- [Installation of Regenerative & Community Development Projects](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/services/installation-community-projects/): Our crews build regenerative and community projects: earthworks, planting and water systems, done right.
- [Farm Solutions](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/services/farm-solutions/): Regenerative farm systems in line with permaculture: agroforestry, syntropic agroforestry, food forests and more.
- [Maintenance](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/services/maintenance/): Seasonal care that keeps your landscape healthy, productive and beautiful.
- [Education for Regenerative Design & Management](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/services/education/): Hands-on training in designing and managing regenerative land, skills your team can use the next day.

## Projects (initiatives Permavia is building; none is complete yet)
- [All projects and their current stage](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/projects/)
- [Million Trees](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/million-trees/): A tree nursery being set up to grow seedlings for farms, homes and restoration sites, with the ambition of millions of trees in the ground.
- [Permavia Farm](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/permavia-farm/): A planned 5-acre living demonstration of regenerative land management: food forests, water systems, practical learning and farm-to-table experiences.
- [Permavia Academy](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/permavia-academy/): Our education platform for regenerative design and management: practical training, online learning and field demonstrations.

## Guides (Regenerative Journal)
- [Harvesting Rain: Simple Water Systems for Ugandan Homes and Farms](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/blog/harvesting-rain-water-systems/): To get water through the dry season in Uganda, slow rainwater down, spread it out and sink it into the soil. Start with roof catchment (a 100 m² roof collects about 1,000 litres for every 10 mm of rain), add swales dug on contour to store water in the soil, and use ponds or infiltration basins where the land allows.
- [Why Landscaping Is More Than Just Beauty](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/blog/why-landscaping-is-more-than-just-beauty/): Regenerative landscaping keeps the beauty of a garden but makes it work for you: fruit trees, perennial vegetables and herbs feed your family, well-placed trees cool your home and block wind, and mulch and groundcover protect the soil, which lowers water, fertiliser and food costs over time.
- [Transforming Spaces: The Art of Green Design](https://www.permavialandscapes.com/blog/transforming-spaces-the-art-of-green-design/): Good green design starts by observing a site (sun, wind, water and how people move) before changing anything. Permaculture then organises the land into zones by how often you visit them, and agroforestry uses trees as the backbone, providing shade, fruit, fodder, timber and mulch while feeding and holding the soil.
